scope: Two measured changes on the unchanged readiness-gated burst and soak profiles, metrics mode (store counters) for every run so pool queue wait is visible. Local only; Docker only via the task socket; forwarder untouched; Tilt :3001 left running (healthy after each middleware edit/install); no cloud.

change1_socketCap.where: The BFF builds the DynamoDB client for DynamoChatStore, pins and membership (middleware/src/lib/realtime-gateway.ts socialChatClient); the library only receives it. SOCIAL_CHAT_MAX_SOCKETS existed (1-256); the bound is now 1-1024 with keepAlive spelled out (already the SDK default). Default unchanged (50).
change1_socketCap.image: orgiq-middleware:cluster-sockets-validation sha256:830115567800094a03b865eb657136d37a5115b16a48575eae04918c5aaf6d7a = the 0.109 image plus a two-line sed overlay of exactly that bound/keepAlive change (overlay/Dockerfile, image-artifact.log), so 50/256/512 differ only by env.
change1_socketCap.finding: Raising the cap removes the pool queue (mean wait 350-410 ms -> 0.3-13 ms; queued peak ~1,200 -> 120-840) but does not improve chat p95 and makes the soak worse (1 CPU: 1,840 -> 2,855 at 256, 4,606 at 512; 2 CPU: 623 (sizing) -> 2,482 / 3,118), adds AUTHZ_CHANNEL_DENIED and protocol errors and raises health p99. The queue was metering concurrency into a BFF whose single JS thread already peaks at ~100% (docker CPU 100-125% is one core plus libuv/GC, not headroom). Recommendation: keep 50.

change2_requestsPerSend.finding: Send-path requests fall 6.7 -> 3.9 and pool wait barely moves because presence/join/notification traffic still fills the 50 sockets. Latency does not improve beyond run-to-run noise at 1 CPU; transaction mode raised DynamoDB Local CPU (peaks 98-158%) and one 1-CPU soak hit 801 DynamoDB errors with 351 fail-closed denials. At 2 CPU both 0.110 soaks pass health (a 38.5/31.3, b 18.9/35.4) and all denial/error targets, but chat p95 stays ~690 ms (sizing 0.109: 623) and memory reads 704-745 MiB (heap limit scales with the 4 GiB container).

runsNote: memPeakMiB/cpuPeak from docker stats; healthP99 [node a, node b]; queuedPeak/meanPoolWaitMs from the Dynamo HTTP agent per node; dynamoRequestsPerSend = all chat-table Dynamo requests (both nodes, transactions included) / persisted sends, so it includes presence/join/notification traffic. invite/accept/chat are p95 ms. 1-CPU runs 1024 MiB; 2-CPU runs 4096 MiB (sizing comparability).
caveats: Every run is a single run; earlier stages show burst chat p95 varies 2.5-4.3 s on an unchanged image. The two 0110 1-CPU plain bursts established 84/100 and 94/100 calls (invite receipts timed out under the burst) while the same config with origin attribution established 100/100; not attributed to a cause.
The library jest gate ran on the host during soak-2cpu-s256 and burst/soak-2cpu-s512.

Origin attribution (ORGIQ_BFF_CONTAINER_ORIGIN_METRICS=1 -> ORGIQ_NATIVE_ORIGIN_METRICS) was added to native-rds-preload.mjs after the 1-CPU socket series; with it off it adds one no-op closure per Dynamo call. Transactions have no top-level TableName, so the per-table maps omit them; summarize_run.py adds them back.
verdict: No configuration passed every target at the deployed 1-CPU size, so there is no candidate for deploy plan section 11. Capacity remains unaccepted.
